title: Statistics Adventure 3: Exam-Style Stretch
welcome_lead: Time to stretch! You'll compare distributions, read box plots, and interpret scatter graphs with lines of best fit.
meta_desc: GCSE Maths Statistics stretch — comparing distributions, box plots, IQR, scatter graphs and correlation.
final_note: You can now compare two data sets using averages and spread, read box plots, and judge correlation on a scatter graph.

walkthroughs.body_html:
When you compare two data sets, always make two comments:

  • An average (mean or median) — which is higher?
  • A measure of spread (range or IQR) — which is more consistent?

Write in context. E.g. "Class A had a higher median score, but Class B's results were more consistent (smaller IQR)."

A box plot shows five key values: minimum, lower quartile (Q1), median, upper quartile (Q3) and maximum.

IQR = Q3 − Q1

The IQR shows the spread of the middle 50% of the data. A smaller IQR means more consistent values.

Scatter graphs plot two variables against each other. The pattern tells you the correlation:

  • Positive — as one goes up, so does the other.
  • Negative — as one goes up, the other goes down.
  • None — points are scattered randomly.

Use a line of best fit to predict. Predictions inside your data (interpolation) are reliable. Outside (extrapolation) — be careful!

mcqs.q: On a box plot, what does the IQR measure?
options: Total range of data
Spread of the middle 50%
The mean
The mode

mcqs.q: A scatter graph shows: as hours of revision rise, test scores rise. What correlation is this?
options: Negative correlation
No correlation
Positive correlation
Zero correlation

mcqs.q: Which average is best to use for the data set [2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 100]?
options: The mode is most affected because the outlier becomes the new most common value.
The median (3.5) — it isn't distorted by the outlier 100, unlike the mean.
The mean — it always gives the most accurate average.
The mode, because the most common value is always the best representative.

mcqs.q: What is the range of the data set [4, 7, 2, 9, 5]?
options: 7 — the largest minus the smallest (9 - 2).
5, because that is the middle value.
The mode is most affected because the outlier becomes the new most common value.
From 2 to 9 — the range is given as two values.

mcqs.q: If a data set has an extreme outlier, which average is most affected?
options: The mode is most affected because the outlier becomes the new most common value.
The mean — because every value (including the outlier) contributes to it.
The median is most affected because the outlier shifts the middle.
The mode, because the most common value is always the best representative.
